Quatorze ateliers, trois siècles, une ma: Fourteen workshops, three centuries, a machine to assemble piece by piece.
Ici, on ne remonte pas le temps pour le: Here, you don't go back in time for fun: you build. Each workshop teaches you an inventor's idea, has you carry it out, and leaves you a piece of the computer. At the end, you switch it on.
Additionner et faire passer la retenue d: Add, and pass the carry from one digit to the next.
À 19 ans, Blaise Pascal fabrique une mac: At 19, Blaise Pascal builds a machine that adds with toothed wheels. When a wheel goes from 9 to 0, a part, the jumper, drops and moves the next wheel on: that is the carry.
Une Pascaline n'a qu'un geste : faire av: A Pascaline has only one move: turning a wheel on by one notch. First enter the first number, wheel by wheel. Then add the second: turn each wheel on by as many notches as its digit. When a wheel goes from 9 to 0, the jumper moves its neighbour on: that is the carry. The result shows up on the wheels by itself.
Écrire tous les nombres, et tout le rest: Write every number, and everything else, with 0s and 1s.
Leibniz écrit les nombres avec deux chif: Leibniz writes numbers with only two digits, 0 and 1. Each position is worth twice its right-hand neighbour: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
Allumez les bonnes cases pour écrire le: Light up the right boxes to write the requested number in binary.
Donner les ordres à la machine sans la r: Give orders to the machine without rebuilding it.
Le métier de Jacquard lit son motif sur: Jacquard's loom reads its pattern from punched cards. Where there is a hole, a needle goes through and lifts a thread; changing the pattern means changing the cards.
Perforez la carte : un trou partout où l: Punch the card: a hole wherever the pattern calls for a raised thread.
Garder les nombres en attendant le calcu: Keep the numbers until the calculation.
Dans la machine analytique de Babbage, l: In Babbage's Analytical Engine, the store keeps the numbers and the mill calculates. Punched cards, borrowed from Jacquard looms, tell the mill which operation to do.
Choisissez les deux cartes d'opération :: Choose the two operation cards: the mill first calculates with the first two numbers in the store, then with the third.
Une suite d'instructions précises, avec: A sequence of precise instructions, with loops.
Dans sa note G, Ada Lovelace écrit, opér: In her note G, Ada Lovelace writes out, operation by operation, the calculation Babbage's engine should carry out. The same cards can be used again several times: her calculation foreshadows the loops of today's programs.
Suivez le programme pas à pas, comme la: Follow the program step by step, like the machine, and give the number displayed at the end.
Faire entrer les données dans la machine: Get data into the machine, by electricity.
Pour le recensement américain de 1890, l: For the 1890 US census, the answers (age, state, sex…) are punched onto cards. In Herman Hollerith's machine, pins go through the holes and dip into mercury: the current flows and moves a counter on. His company, founded in 1896, merges in 1911 into a firm renamed IBM in 1924.
Passez les cartes dans la machine : chaq: Feed the cards through the machine: each hole in the requested column moves the counter on by one notch. Set the counter to the total.
Lire les règles et décider, pas à pas, d: Read the rules and decide, step by step, what to do next.
En 1936, dans son article « On Computabl: In 1936, in his paper "On Computable Numbers", Alan Turing imagines a machine that reads and writes symbols on a tape, square by square, following a table of rules. A universal machine can imitate any other Turing machine whose description it is given.
La machine part de la case la plus à dro: The machine starts from the rightmost square. Rule: a 1 becomes 0 and it moves left; a 0 (or an empty square) becomes 1 and it stops. Write the final tape.
Calculer avec des interrupteurs : ET, OU: Calculate with switches: AND, OR, NOT.
Dans son mémoire de 1937, Claude Shannon: In his 1937 thesis, Claude Shannon calculates relay circuits with Boolean algebra. For current to flow, two switches in series must both be closed (an AND); in parallel, one is enough (an OR). His thesis even describes a base-two adder.
Lisez la table de vérité et choisissez l: Read the truth table and choose the gate that produces it. For a half adder, you need two: one for the sum, one for the carry.
Additionner, soustraire, comparer : du c: Add, subtract, compare: calculation made of gates.
En novembre 1937, George Stibitz, ingéni: In November 1937, George Stibitz, an engineer at Bell Labs, puts together a binary adder from relays, the Model K, named after the kitchen table he is said to have built it on. For one digit, an exclusive-OR gate gives the sum, an AND gate the carry; stages are chained digit by digit. In 1970, Texas Instruments fits a complete arithmetic logic unit on a single chip for the first time: the 74181, which calculates on 4 bits.
Additionnez les deux nombres de 4 bits,: Add the two 4-bit numbers, from right to left, carrying over. The leftmost box gets the last carry: if it is lit, the result no longer fits in 4 bits (an overflow).
Un interrupteur électrique minuscule, de: A tiny electric switch, billions per chip.
En 1944, le Harvard Mark I calcule avec: In 1944, the Harvard Mark I calculates with 3,500 relays: about three additions per second. Vacuum tubes (Fleming's valve in 1904, De Forest's grid in 1907) switch with no moving parts: the ENIAC, inaugurated in 1946, does 5,000 additions per second, but several tubes burn out almost every day. From November 17 to December 23, 1947, at Bell Labs, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain develop the transistor, in William Shockley's group.
Chaque transistor laisse passer le coura: Each transistor lets current through when its input is 1. Say whether the lamp lights up (1) or stays off (0).
Ranger le programme dans la mémoire, ave: Store the program in memory, with the data.
En juin 1945, le premier rapport sur l'E: In June 1945, the first report on the EDVAC, signed by John von Neumann, describes the machine in "organs": an arithmetic unit, a control unit, a memory that keeps both data and instructions, and inputs and outputs. The idea owed a lot to Eckert and Mauchly, the builders of the ENIAC.
Placez chaque organe à sa place sur le p: Put each organ in its place on the plan, according to what it does.
Garder des milliers de bits, chacun à so: Keep thousands of bits, each at its own address.
À l'université de Manchester, Freddie Wi: At the University of Manchester, Freddie Williams and Tom Kilburn store bits as dots on the screen of a cathode-ray tube: each dot carries a small charge, 1 or 0. To read or write, the machine gives an address, a row and a column, and the beam goes straight to that dot: it is a random-access memory, the ancestor of RAM.
Our memory has 8 rows and 8 columns. In the address, the first 3 bits give the row, the last 3 the column (rows and columns counted from 0). Touch the target box.
Chercher, décoder, exécuter, et recommen: Fetch, decode, execute, and start again.
Le 21 juin 1948, la Baby de Manchester e: On June 21, 1948, the Manchester Baby runs a program stored in its memory. The processor endlessly repeats the same cycle: fetch the instruction whose address is in the program counter, decode it, execute it, then move on to the next one, unless the instruction is a jump.
Exécutez le programme comme le processeu: Run the program like the processor: one instruction at a time, in order, except for jumps. CHARGER_A 14 copies box 14 into register A; AJOUTER B A does A ← A + B; SOUSTRAIRE B A does A ← A − B; RANGER_A 13 copies A into box 13; SAUTER 2 goes back to address 2; SAUTER_SI_NÉGATIF 5 only jumps there if A is negative. What does box 13 hold at the end?
Traduire un programme écrit pour les hum: Translate a program written for humans into machine language.
En 1947, à Harvard, un papillon de nuit: In 1947, at Harvard, a moth found in the Mark II ends up taped into the logbook: "First actual case of bug being found". In 1952, Grace Hopper completes the A-0 system, her "A compiler".
Ce petit programme a un bug. Touchez la: This little program has a bug. Touch the faulty line.
Toutes les pièces sont en place, de la r: All the pieces are in place, from Pascal's carry wheel to Grace Hopper's compiler: binary, the cards, the mill, the algorithm, the gates, the arithmetic unit, the transistor, the memory and the processor. All that's left is to press the button.
Bienvenue sur mon chantier. Casque oblig: Welcome to my building site. Hard hat compulsory, brain optional: I see you've made your choice.
Trois siècles d'inventions en dix atelie: Three centuries of inventions in ten workshops. The inventors spent whole lifetimes on them. You have the evening.
Piece in place. It holds. For now.
Correct. L'inventeur aurait été fier, ou: Correct. The inventor would have been proud, or jealous.
Une pièce de plus. La machine commence à: One more piece. The machine is starting to look like you: incomplete.
Raté. Les inventeurs aussi ratent ; eux,: Missed. Inventors miss too; they, at least, took notes.
La pièce ne s'emboîte pas. L'erreur non: The piece doesn't fit. Then again, neither does your mistake.
Un bug s'est glissé dans le chantier. Je: A bug has slipped into the building site. Nothing to do with me. Almost nothing.
Quelque chose grignote vos pièces. Chass: Something is nibbling at your pieces. Chase it out, or it will nest in your memory.
Bug chassé. Grace Hopper l'aurait scotch: Bug chased out. Grace Hopper would have taped it into the logbook.
Plus de bug. Jusqu'au prochain : il y en: No more bugs. Until the next one: there's always a next one.
Le bug est toujours là, et il a pris ses: The bug is still there, and it has made itself at home.
Raté. Le bug vous remercie de votre hosp: Missed. The bug thanks you for your hospitality.
Une pièce est en panne : vous avez oubli: A piece has broken down: you've forgotten how it works. Pass its review to repair it.
Elle s'allume. Une machine qui calcule,: It lights up. A calculating machine, built by you. Don't ask it to think: that's my job.
Allumée. Les points de la Baby dansaient: Switched on. The Baby's dots danced; yours do what they can.
